data.title: A New Frontier in America's Lithium Story: Elektros (OTC PINK:ELEK) Evaluates Northern New York Hard-Rock Opportunity
data.description:
Preliminary property review reflects the company's interest in potential domestic sources of battery materials

WEST PALM BEACH, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 6, 2026 / Looking Closer to Home for Lithium Potential

Lithium has become an important material in the evolving electric-vehicle and energy-storage industries. As manufacturers and supply-chain participants assess the future availability of battery materials, potential sources located in the United States continue to draw attention.

ELEKTROS Inc. , a publicly traded company, is evaluating a potential hard-rock lithium opportunity in northern New York near the Canadian border. The review is preliminary and exploratory. ELEKTROS has not completed or announced an acquisition of the property, and no independently verified mineral resource, mineral reserve or economic development case has been established.

Why a Domestic Opportunity Deserves a Closer Look

If the property's geology, mineral rights, infrastructure, permitting pathway and economics ultimately prove supportive, a viable operation could potentially contribute to a domestic supply option for participants in the battery-material chain. A U.S.-based source could also, in principle, reduce reliance on overseas ocean transport and certain international customs procedures.

Those possibilities remain matters for investigation-not established project advantages. Further work is required to determine whether lithium is present in commercially meaningful quantities and whether development would be practical, permissible and financially supportable.

A Market at an Important Crossroads

Benzinga's October 22, 2026 article, "Lithium's $100 Billion Supply Gap Hands Albemarle a Domestic Moat," referenced a Benchmark Mineral Intelligence outlook projecting that global lithium demand could more than triple by 2050. The outlook described a possible need for 134 new mines and more than $100 billion in investment, with electric-vehicle batteries and stationary energy storage contributing to demand.

These broad industry estimates are not forecasts for ELEKTROS and do not establish the quality, scale or value of the northern New York property. The cited article discussed companies other than ELEKTROS.

EV Charging Technology: A Separate Area of Focus

ELEKTROS is also exploring potential development relationships concerning its multi-port electric-vehicle charging patent, U.S. Patent No. 12,522,100 B1. The company views its charging-technology initiative and its review of lithium opportunities as separate activities within its longer-term areas of interest.

The company is not announcing a completed prototype, patent license, customer deployment, adoption milestone or revenue associated with the patent.

From Possibility to Evidence

Further evaluation of the northern New York possibility may include confirming ownership and mineral rights; obtaining independent geological analysis and sampling; reviewing environmental and permitting requirements; assessing infrastructure and potential processing routes; and evaluating logistics, financing and transaction structure.

Management believes disciplined due diligence is essential before making commitments. Any decision to advance the opportunity will depend on the evidence gathered and management's assessment of technical, regulatory, financial and commercial considerations.

Commitment to Measured Progress

ELEKTROS appreciates the continued engagement of its shareholders and those following developments in North American lithium. The company intends to continue identifying and assessing opportunities while recognizing that early-stage concepts require careful validation before they can be characterized as viable projects.

Management expresses gratitude to Almighty God as the company works toward measurable progress. This release is for informational purposes only and does not constitute an offer to sell securities or a recommendation to purchase ELEK shares.

About ELEKTROS Inc.

ELEKTROS Inc. is publicly traded on the OTC market under ticker symbol ELEK. The company's areas of interest include hard-rock lithium opportunities, EV charging infrastructure and patented EV charging technology. The northern New York property discussed in this release has not been acquired by ELEKTROS and is not a producing mine.

ELEKTROS has not announced a completed acquisition of the northern New York property, an independently verified mineral resource or reserve, a feasibility study, a mining permit, an operating mine, a production schedule, a refinery supply agreement or a commercial charging prototype.

data.title: BP says Whiting, Indiana refinery offered to meet union, awaits response
data.description:
BP on Friday said representatives from its 440,000-barrel-per-day oil refinery in Whiting, Indiana had offered to meet United Steelworkers Local 7-1 next week but had yet to receive confirmation from the union.

"At our last negotiating session on Monday, October 26, BP again provided revised contract language to address union concerns. We had also expected the union to bring revised contract language for consideration, but it did not," the company said in a statement.

data.title: Repligen Shares Fall on $1B Note Issuance
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Repligen shares fell after the company issued $1 billion in convertible senior notes.

Shares were down 20% at $138.99 after-hours on Friday. The stock closed up 3% at $173.49, and was up 5.9% this year through the close.

The company sold the notes with a 0.25% rate and a maturity date of Nov. 1, 2031, according to a Friday filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Around $541.4 million worth of the new notes were issued in exchange for around $456.8 million worth of the company's existing 1% notes due 2028. The remainder was issued for around $458.6 million in cash.

Repligen said it has around $143.2 million worth of the 2028 notes outstanding following the transaction.

data.title: Gold futures pull back as strong U.S. payrolls report boosts dollar, yields
data.description:
Gold gave back a slice of the strong gains of the previous two sessions on Friday, as a larger-than-expected rise in U.S. October payrolls lifted yields and strengthened the dollar while reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December.

The U.S. Labor Department reported non-farm payroll employment rose by 165K in October, substantially ahead of economists' consensus estimates and September's upwardly revised gain of 60K, the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, and average hourly earnings increased 0.4%.

The latest data showing a resilient labor market could provide new momentum for the U.S. dollar, creating another headwind for gold, Forex.com analyst Fawad Razaqzada said in a note.

"This solid employment report should reinforce the Federal Reserve's assessment that the labor market remains solid, potentially stabilizing front-end yields and providing some support for the dollar," Razaqzada wrote.

The jobs report "is not a soft-landing signal for gold—it is a bond-yield signal," CMS Prime's Terri-Leigh Bennett said in a note to Kitco News. "Treasury yields are rising because markets now see an economy that can tolerate restrictive policy for longer."

Traders now see an 81% chance that the Fed will raise rates in December, compared with 73% before the payrolls report, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Front-month Comex gold for November delivery dropped 0.9% to $4,064.50/oz, and front-month Comex November silver slipped 0.81% to $51.803/oz.

For the week, gold and silver gained 4.6% and 5.5%, respectively, in their largest one-week net and percentage increase since the week ending August 21.

data.title: DelphX Closes Non-Brokered Unit Private Placement
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario and New York, New York--(Newsfile Corp. - November 6, 2026) - DelphX Capital Markets Inc. (OTC Pink: DPXCF) ("DelphX" or the "Company"), a leader in the development of new classes of structured products, announces that it has closed the non-brokered private placement announced on October 19, 2026 (the "Offering"). The Company issued 5,500,000 units (the "Units") at a price of C$0.01 per Unit for gross proceeds of C$55,000.

Each Unit consists of one common share of the Company (a "Common Share") and one Common Share purchase warrant (a "Warrant"). Each Warrant entitles the holder to purchase one additional Common Share at an exercise price of C$0.06 until November 6, 2028, two years from the date of issuance.

No finder's fees were paid in connection with the Offering. No insiders of the Company participated in the Offering.

DelphX intends to use the net proceeds of the Offering for general working capital and corporate overhead. The Company does not expect any single specific use to represent 10% or more of the gross proceeds of the Offering. None of the proceeds of the Offering will be paid to Non-Arm's Length Parties of the Company. No more than 10% of the gross proceeds of the Offering will be used to fund investor relations activities.

The Offering remains subject to the final acceptance of the TSX Venture Exchange. The securities issued under the Offering are subject to a hold period expiring March 7, 2027, being four months plus one day from the date of issuance. As the Units were priced at less than C$0.05 per Unit, the securities are also subject to the Exchange Hold Period and are legended accordingly.

Following the closing of the Offering, the Company has 257,210,183 Common Shares issued and outstanding.

About DelphX Capital Markets Inc.

DelphX is a technology and financial services company focused on developing and distributing the next generation of structured products. Through its special purpose vehicle Quantem LLC, the Company enables broker dealers to offer new private placement securities that provide for both fixed income and cryptocurrency solutions. The new DelphX securities will enable dealers and their qualified institutional investors (QIBs) accounts to competitively structure, sell and make markets in:

  • Collateralized put options (CPOs) that provide secured rating downgrade protection for underlying corporate bonds and/or protection from losses in cryptocurrency holdings;

  • Collateralized reference notes (CRNs) that enable investors to take on a capped rating downgrade and/or cryptocurrency loss exposure of an underlying security or cryptocurrency in exchange for attractive returns.

All CPOs and CRNs are fully collateralized and held in custody by US Bank. CPOs and CRNs are proprietary products created and owned by DelphX Capital Markets.

For more information about DelphX, please visit www.delphx.com.

data.title: Quest Diagnostics Pays $13 Million to Settle Illegal Kickback Allegations
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Quest Diagnostics paid about $13 million to the Justice Department to settle allegations that it offered healthcare providers and executives illegal kickbacks.

The kickbacks, allegedly paid for by federal healthcare programs, were meant to generate business referrals to Quest, according to the lawsuit.

The clinical laboratory company allegedly provided free entertainment events for executives between July 2013 and August 2022, offering items or services such as free tickets for suite seats at New York Giants games.

The lawsuit alleged that the company then submitted false claims for lab services that Medicare and New York and New Jersey Medicaid paid for.

Along with the settlement, Quest has entered into a five-year federal Corporate Integrity Agreement with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Department.

"Although we deny any allegations of wrongdoing or violation of the law, over a year ago, in 2025, we agreed to a settlement with the government to put the matter behind us," the company said.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: Moderna Stock Is Up 700% on Cancer Vaccine Hype. Earnings Reveal That Covid Still Counts. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mackenzie Tatananni

Moderna stock has surged eightfold this year on mounting excitement over its experimental cancer vaccine. In reality, the biotech remains largely a Covid-driven story — and as its latest earnings showed, that has been working out just fine.

The Massachusetts-based biotech on Friday posted third-quarter revenue of $1.3 billion, outstripping analysts' calls for $890.3 million. The period is typically Moderna's strongest of the year due to the seasonality of respiratory vaccine sales, which continue to dominate its top line.

Defying forecasts for a loss, the company posted a third-quarter profit of $162 million, reversing a $200 million deficit from a year earlier. Earnings came to 38 cents a share, better than Wall Street expectations for a loss of $1.10 a share.

For the full year, Moderna is now targeting 15% to 25% revenue growth, up sharply from a prior outlook of 10% growth. The updated forecast translates to revenue of around $2.2 billion to $2.4 billion, which should be split roughly evenly between the U.S. and international markets, according to management.

Shares jumped 7.8% to $260.26 on Friday, pacing toward their highest close since December 2021, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Moderna stock had already gained nearly 719% this year, far outpacing the broader market.

Covid-linked products predictably did the heavy lifting in the quarter, with sales for the jumping. Higher Covid vaccine sales abroad fueled a 29% jump in revenue. Geographically, the U.S. accounted for $780 million, with international markets contributing the remaining $533 million.

Moderna attributed these gains to the execution of strategic partnerships with governments in the United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia, while also acknowledging as a five-year agreement with a local manufacturer in Mexico for Covid vaccines, a move the company expects to support recurring revenue as well as market expansion.

Jefferies analyst Andrew Tsai expects expanding international partnerships to easily offset falling U.S. demand. Additional growth could follow if U.S. Covid sales, which have declined steadily over recent quarters, stabilize in the fourth quarter.

While Tsai and others on Wall Street have high hopes for coming clinical trial readouts that could validate Moderna's pipeline, the drugmaker's current-day business continues to center on its respiratory vaccine portfolio.

In August, the Food and Drug Administration cleared Moderna's mRNA-based flu shot, mFlusiva, in adults aged 50 and older, marking the first approval of its kind. Moderna didn't break out sales figures for mFlusiva in the latest quarter, noting only that it was targeting a limited U.S. launch for the coming flu season, as approval occurred after the annual contracting cycle. The shot was separately cleared by regulators in Canada on Thursday alongside a combination mRNA vaccine for flu and Covid.

Analyst attention has lately centered on intismeran autogene, the personalized cancer vaccine Moderna is codeveloping with Merck — particularly readouts for kidney, bladder, and lung cancer expected in the next two years.

The partners are "working toward regulatory submissions and preparing for a potential commercial launch," Moderna said Friday. This reaffirmed pledge comes even after a data leak caused shares to plunge 18% in a single session, narrowly avoiding their worst trading day on record.

The expanded Phase 3 results showed intismeran's efficacy alongside Merck's blockbuster immunotherapy, Keytruda, in patients who were at high risk of their melanoma returning after it had been surgically removed.

In an interview with Barron's after the selloff, Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel said the company was "a bit surprised" by the market reaction, seeing as the data were positive.

"As a business, we focus on science and the patients," Bancel said, adding that Moderna believes intismeran will work "everywhere Keytruda works" and possibly be as big as the world's leading cancer drug.

Jefferies' Tsai anticipates a Biologics License Application submission for intismeran in 2027, seeking permission to market and sell the treatment across state lines. Given intismeran's Breakthrough Therapy designation — a status designed to expedite reviews for life-threatening conditions — approval could come as soon as next year.

Write to Mackenzie Tatananni at mackenzie.tatananni@barrons.com

data.title: Greek Debt Still High, But Falling — Market Talk
data.description: Although Greece's high public debt remains a key rating constraint, its rapid decline continues to strengthen debt sustainability, Fitch Ratings said. The agency affirmed Greece's Long-Term Issuer Default Ratings at BBB with a stable outlook, and the continuing trajectory of the nation's debt is a factor supporting its ratings. The rating is also supported by "exceptionally strong fiscal outturns relative to peers," Fitch added. Greece's general government surplus is forecast to be 0.6% of GDP this year, and the country is expected to have a primary surplus of 3.6%, according to Fitch. (stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com)
